subproblem.title: Fubini–Tonelli on the cylinder (0,1) × A ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} (supplied step 2(b)–(c))
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let A ⊆ ℝⁿ (Euclid n) be Borel. Write ι(t, u) := (t, u_1, …, u_n) ∈ ℝ^{n+1} (Lean WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp u))), z_0 := WithLp.ofLp z 0, tail z := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) ∈ ℝⁿ, and Â := {z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} : z_0 ∈ (0, 1) and tail z ∈ A}. All measures are Lebesgue measure (volume). Then (a) Â is Borel; (b) for every Borel f : ℝ^{n+1} → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_Â f = ∫⁻_{u ∈ A} ∫⁻_{t ∈ (0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du; (c) for every f : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ integrable on Â, ∫_Â f = ∫_{u ∈ A} ∫_{t ∈ (0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2(b)–(c) of the parent's supplied proof (product pieces and the Fubini identity), proved here for an arbitrary Borel A.
Notation. ℝ^m := Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) with Lebesgue measure volume. For z ∈ ℝ^{m+1}: z_0 := WithLp.ofLp z 0 and tail z := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) ∈ ℝ^m. For t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, so that ι(t, x)_0 = t, tail ι(t, x) = x and z = ι(z_0, tail z) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_self_tail, WithLp.ofLp_toLp, WithLp.toLp_ofLp). e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; ê_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1}; e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^n; J x := ι(0, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp x)) for x ∈ ℝ^N. DH(z) := fderiv ℝ H z, and DH(z)ê denotes the tuple a ↦ DH(z) ê_a. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

Proof. Fix n and a Borel set A ⊆ ℝⁿ.
1. (The splitting map.) Define e : ℝⁿ × ℝ → ℝ^{n+1} as the composite of four measurable equivalences: (i) the swap (u, t) ↦ (t, u) (MeasurableEquiv.prodComm); (ii) id × ofLp : ℝ × Euclid n → ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) (MeasurableEquiv.prodCongr (MeasurableEquiv.refl ℝ) (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin n → ℝ)).symm); (iii) the inverse of MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0, which sends (t, p) to Fin.insertNth 0 t p = Fin.cons t p (MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove_symm_apply, Fin.insertNth_zero'); (iv) toLp : (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) → Euclid (n+1) (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin (n+1) → ℝ)). Evaluating the composite, e(u, t) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp u)) = ι(t, u). Being a composite of measurable equivalences, e is a measurable equivalence, in particular a measurable embedding, and its inverse is measurable.
2. (Measure preservation.) Each factor is measure preserving for the volume measures (volume on a product is the product measure): (i) by Measure.measurePreserving_swap; (ii) by MeasurePreserving.prod of MeasurePreserving.id and EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp (Fin n) (ofLp carries volume on Euclid n to the product Lebesgue measure on Fin n → ℝ); (iii) volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0 says piFinSuccAbove is measure preserving, hence so is its inverse (MeasurePreserving.symm); (iv) the inverse of the measure-preserving ofLp on Euclid (n+1) (EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp (Fin (n+1)) with MeasurePreserving.symm). By MeasurePreserving.comp, e is measure preserving from volume on ℝⁿ × ℝ (= volume ⊗ volume, Measure.volume_eq_prod) to volume on ℝ^{n+1}.
3. (Preimage of Â.) For (u, t) ∈ ℝⁿ × ℝ we have e(u, t)_0 = t and tail e(u, t) = u, so e(u, t) ∈ Â iff u ∈ A and t ∈ (0, 1). Hence e⁻¹(Â) = A × (0, 1).
4. (Part (a).) Since e is a bijection, step 3 gives Â = (e⁻¹)⁻¹(A × (0, 1)). The set A × (0, 1) is measurable (A Borel, (0,1) open) and e⁻¹ is measurable, so Â is Borel.
5. (Part (b).) Let f be Borel. By change of variables along the measure-preserving measurable embedding e (MeasurePreserving.setLIntegral_comp_preimage_emb), ∫⁻_Â f dλ^{n+1} = ∫⁻_{e⁻¹(Â)} f(e(p)) d(λⁿ ⊗ λ¹)(p) = ∫⁻_{A × (0,1)} f(e(u, t)) d(λⁿ ⊗ λ¹). The function f ∘ e is measurable, so Tonelli's theorem on the product set (setLIntegral_prod) turns this into ∫⁻_{u ∈ A} ∫⁻_{t ∈ (0,1)} f(e(u, t)) dt du = ∫⁻_{u ∈ A} ∫⁻_{t ∈ (0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du.
6. (Part (c).) Let f be integrable on Â. Integrability transfers along e (MeasurePreserving.integrableOn_comp_preimage): f ∘ e is integrable on e⁻¹(Â) = A × (0, 1) for λⁿ ⊗ λ¹. Change of variables (MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb) gives ∫_Â f = ∫_{A × (0,1)} f(e(u, t)) d(λⁿ ⊗ λ¹), and Fubini's theorem on the product set (setIntegral_prod, using the integrability just proved) gives ∫_{u ∈ A} ∫_{t ∈ (0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du. ∎

subproblem.title: An integrable weight times a test form pulled back by a Lipschitz map is integrable (supplied step 3, third item)
subproblem.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0 (NNReal), H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q L-Lipschitz, S ⊆ ℝⁿ any set, g : ℝⁿ → ℝ integrable on S (Lebesgue measure), and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^Q) a test form (TestFormOn univ n: a smooth n-form with compact support). Then the function z ↦ g(z)·ω(H(z))(DH(z)e_0, …, DH(z)e_{n−1}) is integrable on S, where DH(z) := fderiv ℝ H z and e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (H : Euclid n → Euclid Q) (S : Set (Euclid n)) (g : Euclid n → ℝ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid Q)) n), LipschitzWith L H → IntegrableOn g S → IntegrableOn (fun z => g z * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n) (H z) (fun a => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent's supplied proof, third item (ŵ_i·f_{i,ω} is measurable and bounded by |ŵ_i|·sup‖ω‖·max(1, L_i)^{n+1}, hence integrable), stated for an arbitrary Lipschitz map H.
Notation. ℝ^m := Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) with Lebesgue measure volume. For z ∈ ℝ^{m+1}: z_0 := WithLp.ofLp z 0 and tail z := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) ∈ ℝ^m. For t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, so that ι(t, x)_0 = t, tail ι(t, x) = x and z = ι(z_0, tail z) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_self_tail, WithLp.ofLp_toLp, WithLp.toLp_ofLp). e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; ê_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1}; e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^n; J x := ι(0, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp x)) for x ∈ ℝ^N. DH(z) := fderiv ℝ H z, and DH(z)ê denotes the tuple a ↦ DH(z) ê_a. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

Proof. Put F(z) := ω(H z)(DH(z)e) = ω(H z)(a ↦ DH(z) e_a).
1. (ω is bounded.) ω is smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞), hence continuous, and has compact support. So there is M ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ M for all y ∈ ℝ^Q, where ‖·‖ is the operator norm of continuous alternating maps (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Since ‖ω(y)‖ ≥ 0, M ≥ 0.
2. (Derivative bound.) For every z ∈ ℝⁿ, ‖DH(z)‖ ≤ L (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; at points where H is not differentiable fderiv is 0). Hence, for each a, ‖DH(z) e_a‖ ≤ ‖DH(z)‖·‖e_a‖ = ‖DH(z)‖ ≤ L, because ‖e_a‖ = 1.

For t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, so that ι(t, x)_0 = t, tail ι(t, x) = x and z = ι(z_0, tail z) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_self_tail, WithLp.ofLp_toLp, WithLp.toLp_ofLp). e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; ê_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1}; e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^n; J x := ι(0, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp x)) for x ∈ ℝ^N. DH(z) := fderiv ℝ H z, and DH(z)ê denotes the tuple a ↦ DH(z) ê_a. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

Proof. Fix N, n, G and Ĝ with Ĝ(z) = ι(z_0, G(tail z)) for all z.
1. (Linear pieces.) T : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝⁿ, T z := tail z, and Φ : ℝ × ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1}, Φ(s, x) := ι(s, x), are ℝ-linear (check each coordinate; for Φ split the index by Fin.cases into 0 and succ j). On finite-dimensional spaces they are continuous linear maps (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). The coordinate map π₀ : z ↦ z_0 is the continuous linear map EuclideanSpace.proj 0. Thus Ĝ(z) = Φ(π₀ z, G(T z)) for every z, i.e. Ĝ = Φ ∘ (π₀, G ∘ T).
2. (Norm identity.) For m ∈ ℕ, s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^m: ‖ι(s, x)‖² = s² + ‖x‖² (EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq and Fin.sum_univ_succ). Every z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} equals ι(z_0, T z), so ‖z‖² = z_0² + ‖T z‖².
3. (Part (a).) Let G be L-Lipschitz and M := max(1, L), so 1 ≤ M and L ≤ M. Let x, y ∈ ℝ^{n+1}. Coordinatewise, Ĝ x − Ĝ y = ι(x_0 − y_0, G(T x) − G(T y)), hence ‖Ĝ x − Ĝ y‖² = (x_0 − y_0)² + ‖G(T x) − G(T y)‖² by step 2. Also x − y = ι(x_0 − y_0, T x − T y) (T is linear), so ‖x − y‖² = (x_0 − y_0)² + ‖T x − T y‖². Now (x_0 − y_0)² ≤ M²(x_0 − y_0)² because M² ≥ 1, and ‖G(T x) − G(T y)‖ ≤ L‖T x − T y‖ ≤ M‖T x − T y‖ gives ‖G(T x) − G(T y)‖² ≤ M²‖T x − T y‖². Adding, ‖Ĝ x − Ĝ y‖² ≤ M²‖x − y‖² = (M‖x − y‖)². Both sides being squares of nonnegative numbers, ‖Ĝ x − Ĝ y‖ ≤ M‖x − y‖, i.e. dist(Ĝ x, Ĝ y) ≤ M·dist(x, y). By LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul, Ĝ is M-Lipschitz.
4. (Part (b).) Ĝ(ι(t, u)) = ι(ι(t, u)_0, G(tail ι(t, u))) = ι(t, G(u)), since ι(t, u)_0 = t and tail ι(t, u) = u.
5. (Derivative.) Let G be differentiable at u and put z := ι(t, u), so T z = u. By the chain rule, HasFDerivAt (G ∘ T) (DG(u) ∘ T) z (G is differentiable at T z = u and T is continuous linear). Pairing with π₀ (HasFDerivAt.prodMk) and composing with the continuous linear map Φ gives HasFDerivAt Ĝ (Φ ∘ (π₀ × (DG(u) ∘ T))) z, where Ĝ is rewritten as z ↦ Φ(π₀ z, G(T z)) by step 1. Hence (HasFDerivAt.fderiv) DĜ(z) ζ = ι(ζ_0, DG(u)(T ζ)) for every ζ ∈ ℝ^{n+1}.
6. (Part (c).) Evaluate on the basis vectors, splitting a ∈ Fin (n+1) by Fin.cases. For a = 0: (ê_0)_0 = 1 and T ê_0 = 0 (every coordinate of the tail of ê_0 is [succ j = 0] = 0), so DĜ(z) ê_0 = ι(1, DG(u) 0) = ι(1, 0) = e₀, checking coordinates by Fin.cases. For a = succ b: (ê_{succ b})_0 = 0 and T ê_{succ b} = e_b (coordinate j of the tail is [succ j = succ b] = [j = b]), so DĜ(z) ê_{succ b} = ι(0, DG(u) e_b) = J(DG(u) e_b). Thus a ↦ DĜ(z) ê_a agrees with Fin.cons e₀ (b ↦ J(DG(u) e_b)) at a = 0 (Fin.cons_zero) and at every a = succ b (Fin.cons_succ), which is the asserted equality of tuples. ∎

For t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m: ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, so that ι(t, x)_0 = t, tail ι(t, x) = x and z = ι(z_0, tail z) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_self_tail, WithLp.ofLp_toLp, WithLp.toLp_ofLp). e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1}; ê_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1}; e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^n; J x := ι(0, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp x)) for x ∈ ℝ^N. DH(z) := fderiv ℝ H z, and DH(z)ê denotes the tuple a ↦ DH(z) ê_a. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

Proof. Fix the data as in the statement.
1. (Siblings.) cyl_fubini applied to n and the Borel set A gives: Â' := {z : z_0 ∈ (0, 1), tail z ∈ A} is Borel; for every Borel f ≥ 0, ∫⁻_{Â'} f = ∫⁻_{u∈A} ∫⁻_{t∈(0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du (Tonelli form); and for every real f integrable on Â', ∫_{Â'} f = ∫_{u∈A} ∫_{t∈(0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du (Fubini form). By hypothesis Â = Â'. suspension_map applied to G and Ĝ gives: (a) Ĝ is max(1, L)-Lipschitz because G is L-Lipschitz; (b) Ĝ(ι(t, u)) = ι(t, G u) for all t, u; (c) if G is differentiable at u then a ↦ DĜ(ι(t, u)) ê_a equals Fin.cons e₀ (b ↦ J(DG(u) e_b)) for every t.
